title_en: Afinet to hold Korea-India AI Inclusive Finance Conference in September
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] AI financial company Afinet is discussing ways to expand financial inclusion using artificial intelligence (AI) with financial and academic experts from Korea and India. It will cover everything from AI credit evaluation for ‘thin-filers’ with insufficient credit history to ways to increase accessibility to financial services such as insurance. Affinit (formerly Balance Hero) announced on the 14th that it will hold the ‘Korea-India AI Financial Inclusion Conference’ in a hybrid method connecting Seoul and Gurgaon, India, on September 9. This conference will be co-hosted by Affinit and the South Asia Center of the Asia Research Institute of Seoul National University. It was prepared to examine the growth potential of India's private financial market and fintech industry and to explore ways to expand financial industry exchanges between Korea and India. In particular, it will discuss ways in which private fintech companies can contribute to expanding financial inclusion, focusing on the case of 'TrueBalance', an AI fintech platform operated by Affinit in India. At the conference, the main agenda will be ways to use AI to increase financial accessibility for those who have had difficulty receiving sufficient credit ratings in the existing financial system. title_en: “I sprinted six times for 30 seconds each”… Amazing changes that occurred inside the body
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] Research has shown that even just a few minutes of high-intensity exercise can cause widespread molecular changes associated with health benefits, including a reduced risk of metabolic diseases. Immediately after sprinting six times for 30 seconds each, about a quarter of the proteins measured in the blood changed. However, this is a comparison of the molecular-level response immediately after exercise, and does not mean that short sprints are better for health or can replace long-term moderate-intensity exercise. According to Rockefeller University in the United States on the 13th (local time), a research team led by Paul Cohen, director of the Molecular Metabolism Research Institute, analyzed blood after performing six 30-second sprints and found changes in about a quarter of the measured proteins. On the other hand, immediately after cycling at moderate intensity for 90 minutes, the amount of protein changed was less than 0.25%. The results of the study were published in the international academic journal ‘Cell Reports Medicine.’ The researchers looked at how the proteins and metabolites secreted in the blood change depending on the intensity and duration of exercise. Substances that are secreted into the blood or change in concentration in response to exercise and transmit signals to other tissues are called ‘exerkines.’ As a result of the analysis, the largest immediate change occurred during high-intensity sprinting. title_en: “I created it myself to avoid low-quality AI content”… Personal search engine ‘Marlin’ Nool
summary_en: [GD Net Korea] Amid the flood of so-called 'AI Slop', low-quality content created by artificial intelligence (AI), an AI search engine that directly collects and searches only independent webs that individuals want has emerged. Marlin directly provides web services focused on individual creators, such as portfolios, small art projects, one-person development software, and zines. It is an open source project designed to collect and search. Rather than covering the Internet as a whole like a large search engine, it is a method of separately collecting the web that users consider important and constructing an index. This project is characterized by simplifying the search engine structure as much as possible. After collecting pages on a homepage basis, a small language model reads each site and generates a site name, short description, category, and tag. It was designed to build a searchable database without storing the entire HTML on a large scale or having a complicated re-collection system. The internal structure consists of four components. As the end of solar power facilities approaches, it is predicted that approximately 180,000 tons of waste panels will need to be processed annually by 2040.
